name: Sootwall Survivor's Layered Street Rig
description: A head-to-toe study in functional desperation made personal. The base is a faded rust-orange thermal long-sleeve, its cuffs frayed and re-stitched with mismatched gray thread, worn under a heavily patched canvas work shirt in washed-out olive — two buttons missing, replaced with wire loops. Over that sits a cropped military surplus jacket, originally some corporate gray, now a patchwork of acid-burn scars sealed with strips of self-repair tape in silver and black, the left shoulder reinforced with a salvaged piece of synthrubber insulation cut from a pipe wrap. The collar is lined inside with faux-fur torn from something older and stitched in with obvious care. Cargo pants in dark charcoal, one knee panel replaced with a different fabric entirely — stiff black ripstop — carry four functional pockets plus a zip pouch sewn onto the left thigh. The boots are resoled construction-style ankle boots, the original leather cracked and re-treated with waterproof sealant that's yellowed with age, the toe caps reinforced with salvaged steel plate held by contact adhesive and pop rivets. A wrapped scarf in dirty ivory serves as hood-liner and face mask in one. A salvaged neural port cover — non-functional, stripped from junked chrome — hangs as a pendant, the only ornament.
functionality: Multi-layer thermal retention against acid rain and wind chill. Self-repair tape seals fresh acid burns on the jacket surface. Cargo pockets carry survival kit, tools, and scavenged components. Steel-capped boots protect against debris and chemical puddles. Scarf doubles as respiratory filter in low-grade atmospheric events.
what_it_says: This person has survived long enough to learn what works. The layers are deliberate, the patches are history, and the salvaged port pendant says they're not afraid of the aug world — just priced out of it. Hard-won competence, zero pretension.
manufacturer: Self-assembled; components from Ironfoot surplus, Coldwall seconds, and anonymous the Gray Zone market stalls
story_hooks: The salvaged neural port pendant is actually a functional data-shard housing — and someone very dangerous wants what's stored inside it.
A CorpSec officer stops the wearer for a 'fabric compliance check' — acid-sealed patches technically violate a new Arcturus municipal ordinance, and this could mean impoundment.
Another the Gray Zone dweller recognizes the specific synthrubber patch as having come from a collapsed building where people died — and wants to know how the wearer got it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A layered survival silhouette that reads as practical, worn, and purposefully assembled from scrap. The figure appears armored by necessity rather than design—each piece adding bulk and texture in different directions. The overall impression is of someone who has survived industrial zones and made their kit from what they could salvage and repair. The aesthetic is deliberately unglamorous: honest wear patterns, visible stitching, and mismatched repairs create a texture-heavy visual.
physical_description.fit: Oversized and loose through the torso for layering flexibility; the military jacket sits cropped at the ribs, allowing cargo pants with a straight leg to hang comfortably. Sleeves are slightly long, cuffed and frayed. The scarf wraps high and loose around the neck and shoulders, functional as hood. Boots fit snug at the ankle. Overall: built for movement and protection, not silhouette.
physical_description.primary_material: Faded cotton-blend thermal base; heavy canvas work shirt; military-grade synthetic-cotton blend jacket; 100% ripstop nylon knee panel; treated leather boots with synthetic sealant overlay; salvaged synthrubber insulation patch; self-repair fabric tape; faux-fur collar lining; cotton-linen wrapped scarf
physical_description.texture: Heavily textured and tactile: frayed cuffs, rough self-stitched seams, quilted tape repair lines, acid-scarred fabric, cracked and re-sealed leather, rough pop-riveted steel reinforcement, worn synthrubber that's slightly sticky, the contrasting nap of faux-fur, and the stiffness of industrial ripstop. Surfaces are worn smooth in high-friction areas; edges are deliberately rough.
physical_description.color_scheme: Rust-orange thermal base visible at wrists; faded olive canvas; industrial gray military jacket with silver and black repair tape stripes; dark charcoal cargo pants with a block of black ripstop at the knee; yellowed sealant streaks on leather boots; dirty ivory scarf; matte gray non-functional neural port cover as pendant. No bright colors; an overall palette of exhaustion and rust.
physical_description.closures: Wire loops replacing two buttons on canvas shirt; friction-fit layering; standard cargo pants belt loops; zip pouch on thigh; contact adhesive and pop rivets securing boot reinforcement; scarf wraps and knots casually
distinctive_features: Frayed re-stitched cuffs in mismatched gray thread
Acid-burn scarred military jacket patched with silver and black self-repair tape
Synthrubber pipe-wrap insulation shoulder patch, asymmetrical
Faux-fur lined collar in visible faux-fur
Ripstop knee panel in different fabric, stiff and clearly grafted
Zip pouch sewn directly to left thigh cargo pocket
Four functional cargo pockets plus thigh pouch
Leather boots with yellowed waterproof sealant, cracked
Steel toe plate held by contact adhesive and visible pop rivets
Non-functional salvaged neural port cover worn as pendant/talisman
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 (sub-grade/ungoverned). Every piece signals resource scarcity and self-sufficiency. This is survival wear assembled from industrial surplus and the Gray Zone market finds, not commercial retail.
physical_description.cultural_context: Sootwall district survivor, industrial zone worker, or someone who has lived through environmental hazard and material scarcity. The gear speaks to someone who repairs their own kit, salvages components, and has learned to make one piece do the work of three. The pendant non-functional neural port suggests past contact with chrome culture but current lack of access—kept as reminder or talisman. No corporate affiliation; anti-corpo by default.
physical_description.condition_typical: Perpetually broken-in and patched. This outfit is *meant* to look weathered and actively used. Pristine condition would be a lie. Wear patterns deepen with use; repairs accumulate. Sealant yellows further. Threads come loose and get re-tied. This is gear that ages visibly and honestly.
